notes:
The Embarcadero, north stretch (Bay St to Filbert/Battery), sheet p01. 13 blocks (57, 59, 58, 80, 81, 82, 85, 84, 83, the block south of Filbert west of Montgomery, 107, 108, 109), one open polygon (piers and bay together). Box as assigned.
(1) West side of the Embarcadero: the block faces lie under the heavy C-2/M-1 zoning border (about 6 px thick; street-side edge x 1551 at y 1250, 1597 at 1300, 1689 at 1400, kink near (1710,1423), 1753 at 1500, 1809 at 1600, 1831 at 1640). No thin line shows beside it, so the blocks' thin line is taken as centred under it: block sides set 2 px inside the heavy line's street-side edge (x = 1549 + 0.92 (y - 1250) above y 1423; x = 1829 - 0.557 (1640 - y) below). Blocks 57, 58, 82, 83 take that line as a side; 81's and 108's corners touch it; 109 is cut by it.
(2) Bay side: NO continuous line is printed anywhere in the box; the Embarcadero's paper runs straight into the water between the piers and into the pier 27/29 apron. The only printed pieces of the bay line are the piers' landward faces, all parallel to the Embarcadero: pier 33 (1587,1170)-(1607,1185), pier 31 (1644,1200)-(1687,1246), pier 27/23 corner (1796,1476)-(1815,1505), pier 19 (1835,1542)-(1856,1579), pier 17 (1875,1614)-(1890,1640). The open polygon follows the street-side edge of those faces and straight lines between the piers' landward ends: (1607,1185)-(1644,1200), (1687,1246)-(1796,1476), (1815,1505)-(1835,1542), (1856,1579)-(1875,1614). The longest unprinted stretch is (1687,1246)-(1796,1476), across the open landward side of the pier 29/27 apron (the land between pier 29's north-west side, which starts at pier 31's corner, and pier 27's long side, (1868,1170)-(1796,1476)); the big M-1 is printed there and was ignored.
(3) Width that results (horizontal, page px): about 57-64 px from y 1476 to the box bottom (about 50-55 px across the street); about 141 px at pier 31 (y 1200-1246) and 116 px at pier 33's tip (y 1185), narrowing along the chord to 57 px at pier 27. The north end is therefore twice as wide as the south end; that is what the pier faces give.
(4) The dash-dot pierhead line (x 1930-2200) and the THE EMBARCADERO and M-1 lettering are not ground; they lie inside the street or the open polygon.
(5) Block 85 (x 1560-1626, y 1514-1587): two thin lines 5 px apart (x 1570-1572 and 1575-1577) run north from Filbert to y 1554, closed at the top, with a 2 px paper slit between them (x 1573-1574, y 1555-1587) that opens onto Filbert. Read as a dead-end lane and cut out of the block as street (a 2 px notch). If it is a lot line drawn double, 85 is one solid block.
(6) The 14 px strip x 1801-1815 between block 108 and the small triangle 109 (from the heavy line at y about 1595 down past the box bottom) is a street (Battery St, lining up with the street between the 110/137 columns further south); 109 is a triangle between its own thin west line (x 1816) and the heavy line.
(7) Heavy zoning borders inside streets (Chestnut y 1335-1341, Montgomery x 1620-1627 at y 1340-1426, Lombard y 1419-1426, Greenwich y 1505-1513) and the border stepping through block 85 and the block south of Filbert (x 1587-1609) are zoning lines: they split no block and the strips beside them in the streets are street.
